newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian banks slip on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian banks slip on profit-taking.

text.p: The shares of Australia's four major banks were all weaker at midday on Wednesday due to profit-taking triggered by a weak bond market and less than encouraging comments made by Commonwealth Bank (CBA) chairman, Tim Besley, at the bank's annual meeting on Tuesday.
"We are seeing some profit-taking," said Derek Bond, a senior dealer at Brisbane broker Burrell and Co.
Bond said the local bond market had its first weaker session in six days on Tuesday and was weaker again today.
He said CBA chairman Besley's comments also had been interpreted negatively by the market.

CBA shares were worst affected by the selling. The bank's stock was down 21 cents at A$11.69 at 1.00 p.m. (0300 GMT). National Australia Bank Ltd shares were 16 cents lower at A$13.45, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group stock was eight cents lower at A$7.37 and Westpac Banking Corp shares were down nine cents at A$6.72.
"The bank sector has been pretty hot to trot for a long time now so it's not surprising to see a bit of profit-taking today," Bond said.
